findings.claim: `_resolve_queue` runs unconditionally and unguarded before `readiness_check` is ever invoked (it isn't even defined yet, let alone called, until line 774/786). `_resolve_queue` itself performs the same mirror fetch and default-branch pin (`git_mirror.ensure_mirror`, `package_phase.fetch_default_branch` in cli.py lines 662-666) that `check_readiness`'s 'mirror' and 'default_branch' steps exist to name and report. If the mirror can't be fetched or the origin is unreachable, `_resolve_queue` raises a bare `GitError`/`PackageError` that propagates straight to `main`'s generic exception handler, never reaching `readiness_check`, so the batch dies with an unstructured traceback instead of the 'batch: readiness failed at mirror: ...' message acceptance criterion 9 and `preflight.check_readiness`'s own docstring ('stopping at the first failure and naming it', 'the once-per-run entry point a batch loop calls') promise. The exit code (2) is still correct, but the step-naming contract this spec was written to satisfy is silently bypassed for exactly the infrastructure failures it was built to describe (mirror/origin/default-branch), and `test_a_readiness_failure_names_the_step_that_failed` never catches this because it mocks `_resolve_queue` to always succeed.

`test_the_adapter_stacks_a_child_on_its_parents_branch` and `test_the_adapter_stacks_on_the_first_dependency_only` are the two witnesses the spec names to pin stacking, but both stub `run_one_cell` to raise `SystemExit` immediately, so `_batch_runner`'s packaging branch (lines 586-600) never executes in either test. Neither test — nor any other in this diff — asserts that `target_branch` reaches `package_phase.package(..., parent_branch=target_branch, ...)` inside `_batch_runner`, unlike `_run_cell`'s own packaging call, which an existing test (`captured["parent_branch"] == "saffron/SY-9000"`, test_cli.py:720) does pin. Replacing `parent_branch=target_branch` with `parent_branch=None` in `_batch_runner` reproduces exactly the SA-0026 defect the docstring calls out (a worktree stacked on a parent sha whose PR targets `main`) and both stacking tests, plus the whole suite, stay green.
